questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why it is rude to ask someone's age
The oldest people in Japan
How to look after elderly relatives
How people can live to 100
questions.why: Beth asks, “So how do you live to a hundred?” – that's what they discuss.

questions.q: How does Beth react to Neil's questions about her age?
options: She laughs and tells him
She feels he is being rude
She says she is a centenarian
She asks him the same question
questions.why: She calls it a very personal question, and then says, “That's even ruder!”

questions.q: What did the United Nations estimate in 2021?
options: There were over half a million people aged 100 or more
Most people now live to 100
The number of centenarians is falling
There were only a few thousand centenarians in the whole world
questions.why: Neil says it estimated there were over half a million centenarians worldwide.

questions.q: Which factor for a long life does Neil say is among the most important?
options: Taking vitamins
Living in a warm country
Warm human relationships
Sleeping a lot
questions.why: He says human relationships are among the most important factors for long life.

questions.q: What does Dr Robert Waldinger say about introverts?
options: They live shorter lives
They need to make lots of new friends to stay healthy
They may only need one or two close people
They should avoid pets
questions.why: He says introverts might only need one or two close people, and that's fine for them.

questions.q: According to Dr Waldinger, can healthy relationships be with animals?
options: Yes, pets can give comfort and calm us down
No, they must be with other humans
Only for people who live alone
Only with dogs, and not with cats or any other pets
questions.why: He says it doesn't have to be with another human – pets provide comfort and joy.

questions.q: Which of Dr Nir Barzilai's scenarios does he say is the hardest?
options: Delaying the ageing process
The Peter Pan scenario
Giving young people treatments every year
Making old people young again
questions.why: He says “The Wolverine” or Fountain of Youth, making old people young, is very, very hard.

questions.q: What does the Peter Pan scenario involve?
options: Stopping children from growing up
Regular treatment from your 20s to slow ageing
Giving old people special water
Changing people's diets when they reach the age of 60
questions.why: He describes giving people aged 20 or 30 regular treatments so they age very, very slowly.
